pathway.title: Valaris Ltd — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Revenue visibility is good but concentrated. Contract backlog of USD 4,750.1 million is 2.39x last-twelve-month revenues, yet floaters hold 61.1% of it and four customers supplied 49% of Q3 revenue, so a few customers' programmes decide whether the recovery holds. Basis: calculation K1; calculation F15; calculation F16; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Margins are recovering through operating leverage, and day rates are rising where the fleet is working. Contract drilling expenses fell from 79.1% of revenues in Q1 to 68.4% in Q3 while average daily revenue for floaters rose 19.4% in nine months, so each restarted drillship adds earnings faster than cost; the risk is that jackup day rates fell 2.2% and war-risk insurance cost USD 23.0 million more over nine months, although it eased in the third quarter. Basis: calculation F17; calculation K2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Cash conversion is the weak point. Operating cash flow less capital additions was negative USD 172.7 million in nine months against positive USD 236.8 million a year earlier, and the 2026 capital additions range of USD 445.0 million to USD 470.0 million implies USD 117.0 million to USD 142.0 million more in the fourth quarter, so no debt has been repaid and cash has fallen by USD 74.3 million since year-end to fund maintenance, upgrade and contract-specific spending. Basis: calculation F9; calculation F11; calculation K12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Liquidity is adequate and refinancing is a 2030 question. Liquidity of USD 900.1 million (cash of USD 525.1 million at 2026-09-30, for which a pro forma figure after the October 2026 rig sale is not established, plus the undrawn USD 375.0 million revolver) sits against no principal maturity before 2030, one secured bond of USD 1,100.0 million and a revolver due in 2028 that is undrawn; the revolver becomes a current obligation from April 2027. Its three financial covenants (equity to total assets, interest cover and minimum liquidity) have no levels printed, and the issuer reports compliance in all material respects at 2026-09-30. Basis: calculation F8; calculation F13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 129; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Leverage is moderate and the trajectory is the risk. Reported leverage rose from 1.74x at the end of FY2025 to 2.97x as strong 2025 quarters rolled out of the twelve months, and cover on net interest expense is 3.74x, against cash interest cover of 6.89x in FY2025; trailing leverage falls at the next quarter end if fourth-quarter 2026 reported EBITDA exceeds the USD 80.0 million of the quarter it replaces, and the third quarter was USD 48.6 million above that. Basis: calculation F1; calculation F3; calculation F12; calculation F20; calculation K10; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Governance risk is event-driven rather than extractive. There is no sponsor, no dividend and no repurchase in 2026, but a change of control is scheduled for closing on or about 2026-12-01 and ARO may call up to USD 1,100.0 million of newbuild funding; the notes' fair value of 102.3% of principal sits above the 101.0% repurchase price, so that protection would matter only if the price fell. Basis: calculation F18; calculation F19; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- A one-year return to the first-quarter earnings level would raise net leverage to 3.08x on Adjusted EBITDA, or 3.28x on reported EBITDA, but would not exhaust liquidity. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 266.8 million, the coupon and last-twelve-month capital additions give a cash outflow of USD 259.6 million, leaving liquidity of USD 640.5 million; the scenario is illustrative and ignores cash taxes, working capital, disposals, interest income and any ARO call. Basis: calculation K3; calculation K4; calculation K6; calculation K7; calculation K8; calculation K11

cells.text: Global offshore contract driller with ultra-deepwater drillships and premium jackups, working on day rate contracts in almost every major offshore market
Revenue depends on rig utilisation and day rates, which follow customers' offshore spending rather than the oil price directly

13 drillships and 28 jackups owned at 2026-11-03, plus a 50% interest in ARO, which owns nine rigs; 10 drillships and 17 jackups are active, 3 drillships and 4 jackups are stacked and 7 jackups are leased to ARO
Stacked rigs are an option on recovery but carry reactivation cost; leased rigs earn bareboat charter income from a related party
Day rate contracts; remaining durations about 1 month to 4 years; some contracts can be ended for convenience or if a final investment decision is not taken
Backlog is not a guaranteed cash flow and some of it depends on customer project decisions
USD 4,750.1 million at 2026-11-02: floaters 61.1%, jackups 24.6%, other 14.3% (calculation C4); excludes ARO's own backlog of USD 2,198.6 million
Floaters dominate visible revenue, so drillship day rates and restarts drive the recovery
Fleet utilisation 67% in Q3 2026 against 61% in Q2; revenue efficiency 97%; active drillship utilisation 80%
Rising utilisation lifts revenue faster than costs when the cost base is largely fixed
Contract drilling expenses were USD 379.9 million in Q3 against USD 380.4 million in Q2 while revenues rose to USD 555.6 million, a cost ratio of 68.4% against 75.7% (calculation C8)
Operating leverage lifts margins on recovery and works against margins if utilisation falls
Q3 2026 revenue: BP 15%, Petrobras 13%, Azule 11%, Equinor 10% (calculation C5)
Concentration makes earnings sensitive to a few customers' programmes
Q3 2026 revenue in USD millions: Brazil 137.1, Angola 103.8, United Kingdom 93.4, Gulf of America 72.5; 86% of FY2025 revenue was outside the United States
Brazil is the largest single exposure; tax and political events in a few countries matter
Operating income was reduced by about USD 24.0 million in Q3 and USD 62.0 million in nine months, from shipyard delays on two jackups and war-risk insurance
A further escalation could raise costs and delay ARO work
50/50 joint venture with Saudi Aramco that owns nine jackups and leases seven from Valaris on bareboat charters
ARO is a source of earnings volatility and a contingent funding claim

runs.text: Strengths, ranked by weight in the credit view:

- Contracted earnings base. Backlog of USD 4,750.1 million, all ten active drillships on contract and revenue efficiency of 97% in Q3 mean the recovery rests on signed contracts, which supports debt service over several years; floaters and a handful of customers carry most of it. Basis: calculation K1; calculation F15; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11

- Liquidity and maturity profile. Liquidity of USD 900.1 million and no principal due before the 2030 notes leave time to complete the recovery without refinancing pressure. Basis: calculation F8; calculation F13; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Operating leverage on restarted rigs. The cost ratio fell from 79.1% to 68.4% in two quarters and floater day rates rose 19.4%, so each further restart adds earnings faster than cost. Basis: calculation F17; calculation K2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42

- No sponsor extraction. No controlling shareholder is disclosed, no dividends have been paid and repurchases are paused until closing, which removes the usual leakage route, though it also removes any equity backstop. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70
Weaknesses, ranked by weight in the credit view:

- Negative free cash flow. Capital additions exceed operating cash flow, so cash falls and leverage depends on earnings alone to improve. Basis: calculation F9; calculation F11; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Customer, segment and country concentration. Four customers supplied about 49% of Q3 revenue, floaters hold 61.1% of backlog and Brazil supplied 23.1% of revenue, so one programme or tax event moves results. Basis: calculation F15; calculation F16; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Contingent affiliate funding. Valaris may be asked for up to USD 1,100.0 million of newbuild funding if ARO cannot raise third-party finance; ARO held USD 32.1 million of cash at 2026-09-30, has paid no cash to its partners since formation and owes Valaris USD 400.7 million of notes due in October 2027 and October 2028, so cash may flow out before any flows in. Basis: calculation F19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54

- Event and information risk. The combined company's treatment of the notes is not established, and the issuer will not hold earnings calls or update guidance before closing, so monitoring relies on filings. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 5

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Valaris and Transocean Ltd. signed a business combination agreement on 2026-02-09 under which Transocean will acquire all Valaris common shares for 15.235 Transocean shares each, by court-approved scheme of arrangement under Bermudian law; the value was about USD 5.8 billion at announcement and Valaris holders would own about 47% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis. Regulatory approvals have been received, shareholder meetings are scheduled for 2026-11-24, a Bermuda court hearing for 2026-11-26 and closing on or about 2026-12-01, and either party may end the agreement if it has not closed by 2027-02-09, subject to extension. Until closing the agreement restricts new debt, dividends, repurchases, encumbrances and disposals, and Valaris owes Transocean USD 173.0 million if the agreement ends in specified circumstances, with reimbursement of up to USD 58 million of Transocean expenses if Valaris holders fail to approve. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 154; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

No new debt was issued or repaid in 2026. The capital structure is the USD 1,100.0 million 8.375% second lien notes due 2030-04-30, issued in April and August 2023 by Valaris Limited and Valaris Finance Company LLC and guaranteed by certain subsidiaries, and an undrawn USD 375.0 million revolver due 2028-04-03. Two supplemental indentures were signed on 2026-07-16 and 2026-09-14 and filed as exhibits, naming further Valaris subsidiaries as parties; the documents do not state their purpose. If a change of control triggering event occurs, the issuers may be required to offer to repurchase the notes at 101.0% of principal, but the definition of that event is in the indenture, which was not supplied. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61

The recovery is therefore operating-led, with revenue efficiency of 97% in Q3, but only the last two quarters show it; the trailing measures should improve as the weak Q4 2025 (Adjusted EBITDA of USD 97.0 million) leaves the last twelve months, if Q4 2026 comes in above that level.

The unconsolidated ARO joint venture is a contingent call on cash: each partner may be asked for up to USD 1.1 billion of newbuild funding if ARO cannot raise third-party finance, and USD 400.7 million of notes receivable from ARO are due in October 2027 and October 2028 with an expected extension.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Valaris is a widely held offshore driller with no controlling shareholder disclosed in the supplied documents, so creditors' main exposure is event risk from the pending all-stock sale to Transocean and from the ARO joint venture, not sponsor extraction. A change of control may let holders of the USD 1,100.0 million second lien notes require repurchase at 101.0% of principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating base supports debt service for now: contract backlog was USD 4,750.1 million on 2026-11-02, all ten active drillships are on contract, and no shares have been repurchased in 2026 after USD 425.0 million between 2023 and 2025. Four customers each supplied at least 10% of Q3 revenue, and Middle East conflict costs cut Q3 operating income by about USD 24.0 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership offers creditors neither a sponsor backstop nor sponsor leakage. Valaris emerged from bankruptcy in 2021, has paid no dividends, had 63 holders of record in February 2026, and the supplied documents describe no dividend recapitalisation, liability management transaction or related-party fee other than its lease agreements with ARO; the repurchase programme used USD 425.0 million of its USD 600.0 million authorisation, and the source does not state how the repurchases were funded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The pending Transocean combination is the principal credit event, and its effect on the notes is not established. The all-stock agreement signed on 2026-02-09 values Valaris at about USD 5.8 billion at announcement, leaves Valaris holders with about 47% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis, and is scheduled to close on or about 2026-12-01; until then the agreement restricts new debt, dividends, repurchases, encumbrances and disposals, and Valaris owes Transocean USD 173.0 million if it ends in specified circumstances. The supplied documents do not say how Valaris debt is treated, and the notes' quoted fair value at 2026-09-30 was 102.3% of principal, above the 101.0% repurchase price, so a repurchase offer would help holders only if prices fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Contract backlog gives revenue visibility but rests mainly on floaters. Floaters hold 61.1% of the USD 4,750.1 million backlog, remaining contract durations run from about 1 month to 4 years, and some contracts allow termination for the customer's convenience or if a final investment decision is not taken.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against the view that extraction risk is low is the USD 425.0 million repurchased since 2023 while USD 1,100.0 million of secured notes stayed outstanding, together with USD 175.0 million of programme capacity that remains authorised; the funding source is not stated and the combined company's capital policy is not established. The view would also change if the indenture shows that the notes are repaid, exchanged or left behind a larger secured claim after closing, if a change of control triggering event occurs, if ARO calls capital or its notes receivable are not extended, or if repurchases resume after closing.

fields.value: - Directors, executive compensation and security ownership are incorporated from a proxy statement that was not supplied, so the finding that no controlling shareholder is disclosed could change if a large holder exists.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - ARO's own financial statements are not supplied beyond a condensed income statement, so the finding that the ARO funding commitment is contingent rather than probable cannot be tested against ARO's cash needs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Valaris and Transocean Ltd. signed a business combination agreement on 2026-02-09 under which Transocean will acquire all Valaris common shares for 15.235 Transocean shares each, by court-approved scheme of arrangement under Bermudian law; the value was about USD 5.8 billion at announcement and Valaris holders would own about 47% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis. Regulatory approvals have been received, shareholder meetings are scheduled for 2026-11-24, a Bermuda court hearing for 2026-11-26 and closing on or about 2026-12-01, and either party may end the agreement if it has not closed by 2027-02-09, subject to extension. Until closing the agreement restricts new debt, dividends, repurchases, encumbrances and disposals, and Valaris owes Transocean USD 173.0 million if the agreement ends in specified circumstances, with reimbursement of up to USD 58 million of Transocean expenses if Valaris holders fail to approve.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new debt was issued or repaid in 2026. The capital structure is the USD 1,100.0 million 8.375% second lien notes due 2030-04-30, issued in April and August 2023 by Valaris Limited and Valaris Finance Company LLC and guaranteed by certain subsidiaries, and an undrawn USD 375.0 million revolver due 2028-04-03. Two supplemental indentures were signed on 2026-07-16 and 2026-09-14 and filed as exhibits, naming further Valaris subsidiaries as parties; the documents do not state their purpose. If a change of control triggering event occurs, the issuers may be required to offer to repurchase the notes at 101.0% of principal, but the definition of that event is in the indenture, which was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. The level is driven by the pending change of control and the ARO funding exposure, because both can move cash or ownership away from the current creditor position, which implies event risk rather than extraction risk. Countervailing evidence is the absence of a sponsor, of dividends and of any documented liability management transaction. Further analysis requires the indenture, the credit agreement and the acquirer's disclosure.

fields.value: Valaris Ltd (issuer id val), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the fundamental credit profile of the consolidated group, built on the supplied filings and releases and the earlier modules' findings, with its strongest support, weakest dimension and primary downside path.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Valaris presents an adequate fundamental credit profile: a contracted drillship recovery and USD 900.1 million of liquidity outweigh rising trailing leverage, but negative free cash flow and a pending change of control mean creditors should expect liquidity to erode before earnings fully recover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F8; calculation F6; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Last-twelve-month reported leverage was 2.97x and net debt was USD 563.4 million, or USD 555.9 million pro forma for the October 2026 rig sale; net leverage was 1.54x, or 1.51x pro forma. Operating cash flow less capital additions was negative USD 172.7 million in the first nine months of 2026, which is why a quarter of Adjusted EBITDA of USD 150.6 million, more than twice the first quarter's USD 66.7 million, matters more than the trailing ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation F4; calculation F5; calculation F9; calculation F7; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue visibility is good but concentrated. Contract backlog of USD 4,750.1 million is 2.39x last-twelve-month revenues, yet floaters hold 61.1% of it and four customers supplied 49% of Q3 revenue, so a few customers' programmes decide whether the recovery holds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K1; calculation F15; calculation F16; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margins are recovering through operating leverage, and day rates are rising where the fleet is working. Contract drilling expenses fell from 79.1% of revenues in Q1 to 68.4% in Q3 while average daily revenue for floaters rose 19.4% in nine months, so each restarted drillship adds earnings faster than cost; the risk is that jackup day rates fell 2.2% and war-risk insurance cost USD 23.0 million more over nine months, although it eased in the third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F17; calculation K2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash conversion is the weak point. Operating cash flow less capital additions was negative USD 172.7 million in nine months against positive USD 236.8 million a year earlier, and the 2026 capital additions range of USD 445.0 million to USD 470.0 million implies USD 117.0 million to USD 142.0 million more in the fourth quarter, so no debt has been repaid and cash has fallen by USD 74.3 million since year-end to fund maintenance, upgrade and contract-specific spending.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F9; calculation F11; calculation K12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is adequate and refinancing is a 2030 question. Liquidity of USD 900.1 million (cash of USD 525.1 million at 2026-09-30, for which a pro forma figure after the October 2026 rig sale is not established, plus the undrawn USD 375.0 million revolver) sits against no principal maturity before 2030, one secured bond of USD 1,100.0 million and a revolver due in 2028 that is undrawn; the revolver becomes a current obligation from April 2027. Its three financial covenants (equity to total assets, interest cover and minimum liquidity) have no levels printed, and the issuer reports compliance in all material respects at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F8; calculation F13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 129; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is moderate and the trajectory is the risk. Reported leverage rose from 1.74x at the end of FY2025 to 2.97x as strong 2025 quarters rolled out of the twelve months, and cover on net interest expense is 3.74x, against cash interest cover of 6.89x in FY2025; trailing leverage falls at the next quarter end if fourth-quarter 2026 reported EBITDA exceeds the USD 80.0 million of the quarter it replaces, and the third quarter was USD 48.6 million above that.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F1; calculation F3; calculation F12; calculation F20; calculation K10; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance risk is event-driven rather than extractive. There is no sponsor, no dividend and no repurchase in 2026, but a change of control is scheduled for closing on or about 2026-12-01 and ARO may call up to USD 1,100.0 million of newbuild funding; the notes' fair value of 102.3% of principal sits above the 101.0% repurchase price, so that protection would matter only if the price fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F18; calculation F19; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - A one-year return to the first-quarter earnings level would raise net leverage to 3.08x on Adjusted EBITDA, or 3.28x on reported EBITDA, but would not exhaust liquidity. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 266.8 million, the coupon and last-twelve-month capital additions give a cash outflow of USD 259.6 million, leaving liquidity of USD 640.5 million; the scenario is illustrative and ignores cash taxes, working capital, disposals, interest income and any ARO call.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K3; calculation K4; calculation K6; calculation K7; calculation K8; calculation K11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against an adequate profile is cash conversion: free cash flow has been negative for the last twelve months while capital additions run well above operating cash flow, trailing leverage has climbed to 2.97x, and the Middle East conflicts, shipyard delays and war-risk insurance still cut operating income by about USD 24.0 million in the third quarter. The view would weaken if fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA fell back toward the first-quarter level of USD 66.7 million, if capital additions came in above USD 142.0 million for the quarter, if ARO called capital, or if the change of control left the notes in a weaker position. It would strengthen if earnings held near the third-quarter level and the combined company kept the 2026 pause on repurchases.

fields.value: - Cash interest paid is stated only for fiscal years, so interest cover for the latest period rests on net interest expense, which can differ from cash paid, so the cover finding is approximate.

fields.value: - Ratings, peer data and market prices other than the quarter-end fair value of the notes were not supplied, so the finding that the profile is adequate is judged against the issuer's own history and sector description, not against peers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The shareholder meetings scheduled for 2026-11-24 and the court hearing scheduled for 2026-11-26 fall after the as-of date, so the view describes the pre-closing structure and would need to be redone on the combined group if the transaction closes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths, ranked by weight in the credit view:

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Contracted earnings base. Backlog of USD 4,750.1 million, all ten active drillships on contract and revenue efficiency of 97% in Q3 mean the recovery rests on signed contracts, which supports debt service over several years; floaters and a handful of customers carry most of it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K1; calculation F15; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity and maturity profile. Liquidity of USD 900.1 million and no principal due before the 2030 notes leave time to complete the recovery without refinancing pressure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F8; calculation F13; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Operating leverage on restarted rigs. The cost ratio fell from 79.1% to 68.4% in two quarters and floater day rates rose 19.4%, so each further restart adds earnings faster than cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F17; calculation K2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No sponsor extraction. No controlling shareholder is disclosed, no dividends have been paid and repurchases are paused until closing, which removes the usual leakage route, though it also removes any equity backstop.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses, ranked by weight in the credit view:

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Negative free cash flow. Capital additions exceed operating cash flow, so cash falls and leverage depends on earnings alone to improve.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F9; calculation F11; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer, segment and country concentration. Four customers supplied about 49% of Q3 revenue, floaters hold 61.1% of backlog and Brazil supplied 23.1% of revenue, so one programme or tax event moves results.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F15; calculation F16; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Contingent affiliate funding. Valaris may be asked for up to USD 1,100.0 million of newbuild funding if ARO cannot raise third-party finance; ARO held USD 32.1 million of cash at 2026-09-30, has paid no cash to its partners since formation and owes Valaris USD 400.7 million of notes due in October 2027 and October 2028, so cash may flow out before any flows in.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Event and information risk. The combined company's treatment of the notes is not established, and the issuer will not hold earnings calls or update guidance before closing, so monitoring relies on filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Valaris contracts ultra-deepwater drillships and premium jackups on day rate contracts, so earnings follow rig utilisation and day rates, and a stacked or idle rig earns nothing while its holding costs continue. The group is widely held with no sponsor, which means no committed equity support and no sponsor-driven leakage; the creditors' main exposure is the pending sale to Transocean and the 50% ARO joint venture, which Valaris does not consolidate, so ARO's own debt is outside group net debt and its earnings reach Valaris only as an equity share that Adjusted EBITDA excludes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is contracted for periods of about 1 month to 4 years, which gives visibility, but some contracts allow termination for the customer's convenience or if a final investment decision is not taken, so backlog is not guaranteed cash. Pricing is improving for floaters (average daily revenue up 19.4% over nine months) and softer for jackups (down 2.2%). For creditors, the recovery in revenue is a contracted-restart story whose realisation depends on customers' programmes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_val-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs look largely fixed once a rig is working, so margins widen as utilisation rises and would narrow just as fast if it fell; contract drilling expenses were USD 379.9 million in Q3 against USD 380.4 million in Q2 while revenues rose from USD 502.3 million to USD 555.6 million. Over nine months expense was flat because USD 67.3 million of higher repair and maintenance cost and USD 23.0 million of higher insurance, mainly war-risk cover, were offset by USD 103.8 million of lower costs for rigs sold. Margins can be defended on volume only while utilisation stays high, and the creditor consequence is higher earnings sensitivity in both directions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F17; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is high while idle drillships are returned to work and upgraded: nine-month capital additions of USD 328.0 million were more than twice operating cash flow of USD 155.3 million, and part of that spending is contract-specific and recoverable from customers. Operating cash flow also included about USD 43.0 million of U.S. tax refunds and asset sales brought in USD 102.6 million, while the interest on the notes is fixed. EBITDA is therefore not converting to free cash flow now, and spending is met from cash and asset sales rather than from retained earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F10; calculation F9; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is strong because contracts are awarded by competitive bid and price is often the deciding factor, and ten drillships across the industry were idle at the end of the third quarter with nine due back to work by early 2027, which could cap day rates; the supply of benign environment floaters has fallen by more than 45% since 2014, which supports them. New entry is limited by high newbuild cost and shipyard capacity, substitutes are other oil supply such as onshore shale and, over time, the energy transition, buyers are a few large oil companies with termination rights, and suppliers (shipyards, insurers, crews) have pushed costs up. Politically, the Middle East conflicts cost about USD 24.0 million of operating income in Q3, and tax disputes and the 15% Bermuda tax add earnings uncertainty.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the method's nine dimensions the assessment is: scale and market position average, with a fleet the issuer describes as among the largest in the world (13 drillships and 28 jackups owned at 2026-11-03) but a concentrated customer base; competitive advantage average, resting on modern seventh-generation drillships (12 of 13) rather than on contract terms; business diversification weak to average, with floaters 61.1% of backlog; cost and capex flexibility average, because contract-specific capital spending is recoverable but a fixed cost base is not; margin stability average, improving; free cash flow stability weak; ability to refinance average, with one bond due in 2030 and market quotations not supplied beyond the quarter-end fair value; liquidity position strong relative to maturities; and financial policy and governance average, with no sponsor but event risk from the combination. Supports are the contracted base and liquidity; the main constraint is free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F15; calculation F8; calculation F9; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the debt-service case depends on drillship restarts continuing: management says day rates are moving higher and deepwater opportunities are converting to contracts. Reinvestment stays high, with USD 117.0 million to USD 142.0 million of capital additions still implied for the fourth quarter, and ARO has ordered four newbuild jackups that Valaris may be asked to help fund. Sector tailwinds are customer emphasis on energy security and deepwater sanctioning (about 65% of expected deepwater activity has breakeven prices below USD 50 a barrel), and headwinds are the Middle East conflicts, cost inflation and war-risk insurance. Over three to five years the 2028 revolver and the 2030 notes fall due, so the outlook for earnings through 2027 decides refinancing terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F11; calculation F19; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_a09302026ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: An issuer-specific downside starts with a customer programme delay or a Middle East shipyard stoppage that returns Adjusted EBITDA to the first-quarter level of USD 66.7 million a quarter; at that level revenue and utilisation fall first, the largely fixed cost base turns the margin gain back, and free cash flow turns more negative because capital additions are committed. Holding that level for four quarters gives Adjusted EBITDA of USD 266.8 million, a coupon cover of 2.90x and a cash outflow of USD 259.6 million after the coupon and capital additions, so cash falls from USD 525.1 million at 2026-09-30 to USD 265.5 million, liquidity to USD 640.5 million and net leverage rises to 3.08x. Management can slow discretionary capital additions and sell stacked rigs, as it did in 2026, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within twelve months, but the margin for the 2028 revolver renewal narrows and the revolver's covenants, whose levels are not printed, could become the binding constraint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K3; calculation K4; calculation K5; calculation K6; calculation K7; calculation K8; calculation K9; calculation F7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Valaris presents an adequate business profile supported by contracted drillship backlog, modern assets and liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by negative free cash flow, trailing leverage that has risen and concentration in customers and floaters. Cash-flow durability appears adequate only if the third-quarter earnings level holds. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings through 2027 and on how the change of control treats the notes. The primary downside path is a fall back to first-quarter earnings while capital spending stays committed. Further analysis would require the indenture, the credit agreement, the acquirer's disclosure and ARO's accounts. Fundamental credit review completed with limitations. Top risk: negative free cash flow combined with event risk from the change of control.
